papers.title: Autophagic degradation of RAB8A promotes ferroptosis through dysregulation of TFRC-mediated iron uptake.
papers.summary: Ferroptosis is an iron-dependent cell death driven by lipid peroxidation. The authors identify RAB8A as a selective autophagic substrate and negative regulator of ferroptosis: ferroptotic stress triggers RNF126-dependent ubiquitination and SQSTM1-mediated degradation of RAB8A. RAB8A loss impairs TFRC clearance, boosting iron uptake and lipid peroxidation. RAB8A depletion sensitizes cancer cells to ferroptosis and enhances ferroptosis-inducing therapy in xenografts. RAB8A is upregulated in pancreatic cancer and linked to poor prognosis.

papers.title: Thyroid hormone promotes lipid droplet remodeling and lipophagy through KAT2B/PCAF-dependent histone acetylation in preimplantation embryos.
papers.summary: This study examines how thyroid hormone (T3) regulates lipid droplet remodeling in preimplantation embryos. Transcriptomic profiling revealed metabolic differences between in vivo and in vitro embryos. T3 supplementation enhanced blastocyst formation, reduced lipid droplet size, and increased lipid-mitochondria colocalization. These effects required the histone acetyltransferase KAT2B/PCAF; inhibiting it abolished T3 gains, reduced H3K9ac/H3K27ac, and caused nonselective autophagic stress rather than lipophagy. T3 promoted cytosolic lipolysis, mitochondrial fatty acid import, and mitochondrial membrane potential via KAT2B.

papers.title: Non-cell autonomous control of presynaptic remodeling by the hypothalamic autophagy-NPY axis.
papers.summary: This study examines whether autophagy and neuropeptide Y (NPY) interact within hypothalamic NPY+/AgRP+ neurons to regulate presynaptic organization in distant brain regions. The authors show autophagy in these neurons non-cell autonomously controls hippocampal presynaptic active zone architecture and proteostasis while maintaining NPY levels. Dietary spermidine restored NPY expression in aged hippocampus, suggesting potential to rejuvenate neuropeptide signaling and linking metabolic state to synaptic resilience.

papers.title: Integrating genetic, historical, and demographic evidence to reconstruct Argentina's matrilineal ancestry.
papers.summary: This study integrates genetic, historical, and demographic data to reconstruct Argentina's matrilineal ancestry. Assembling 7,431 mitochondrial haplogroups at the provincial level, the authors found an overall maternal composition of 75% Native American, 22% Eurasian, and 3% African, with significant regional and interprovincial heterogeneity. The work highlights the value of matrilineal markers in admixed societies and stresses the need to rigorously contextualize genetic results given Argentina's demographic and historical complexity.

papers.title: Genomic signatures of selection are enriched in differentially expressed genes in sticklebacks adapting to contrasting environments.
papers.summary: This study tests whether differentially expressed genes are enriched in regions of genetic divergence in sticklebacks adapting to marine versus freshwater environments. Transcriptomics of brain and gill from wild fish showed differentially expressed genes in freshwater populations harbor SNPs previously linked to rapid adaptation and Fst outliers, mostly in cis-regulatory regions. Notable genes include pval4b (gill calcium regulation) and acsl4a (brain fatty acid metabolism). This bridges genomic divergence and molecular mechanisms of physiological adaptation.

papers.title: TRIM26 triggers ferroptosis via ZEB1 degradation to suppress nasopharyngeal carcinoma progression.
papers.summary: This study examines TRIM26, an E3 ubiquitin ligase, in nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) and ferroptosis. TRIM26 was downregulated in NPC cells; its overexpression inhibited viability, migration, and invasion while promoting ferroptosis (increased lipid peroxidation, MDA, Fe2+; reduced GSH, GPX4, SLC7A11). TRIM26 ubiquitinated ZEB1, accelerating its degradation; ZEB1 directly regulated SLC7A11 transcription. ZEB1 overexpression reversed TRIM26-induced ferroptosis, and in xenografts TRIM26 inhibited tumor growth, partially attenuated by ZEB1 co-expression.

papers.title: Early effects of X-ray irradiation on rat incisor periodontal ligament morphology and MMP-2 expression.
papers.summary: This study examines early radiation-induced changes in the periodontal ligament (PDL) of rat incisors after a single 15 Gy head X-ray dose. Irradiation caused progressive fibroblast injury, collagen disorganization, and loss of ECM architecture from day 4. Picrosirius red analysis showed reduced type I-to-type III collagen ratio on days 4, 9, and 14. MMP-2 expression rose significantly at day 4, peaked at day 9, then declined at days 14 and 25, documenting early morphological and matrix changes.

papers.title: Therapeutic potential of an ethnoveterinary formulation against Staphylococcus aureus-induced mastitis via modulating TLR-2/NOX-2 pathway.
papers.summary: This study evaluates an ethnoveterinary oil (EO) formulation against Staphylococcus aureus-induced mastitis in rats. GC-MS identified 21 bioactive compounds, predominantly erucic acid plus phenolics, fatty acid derivatives, terpenoids, and steroidal constituents. EO restored endogenous antioxidant enzymes, reduced lipid peroxidation, myeloperoxidase, and N-acetyl-β-D-glucosaminidase activity, indicating reduced neutrophil infiltration and epithelial protection. It suppressed pro-inflammatory cytokines and downregulated TLR-2 and NOX-2 gene expression, suggesting modulation of a key inflammatory pathway as an alternative treatment strategy.

papers.title: Lineage-Driven Understanding of Human Pericyte Heterogeneity in Vascular Modeling and Regeneration.
papers.summary: This review presents a unified framework of pericyte heterogeneity integrating anatomical distribution, molecular signaling, and embryonic lineage. Pericytes are heterogeneous across organs: brain and retina show high density and near-continuous mural coverage, while skeletal muscle is sparsely invested. CNS pericytes control blood-brain barrier integrity, whereas peripheral pericytes participate in vascular remodeling. Trunk/visceral pericytes arise from mesoderm, cranial/forebrain pericytes from neural crest; neural crest-derived pericyte-like cells induce BBB phenotypes more effectively. Lineage is proposed as a primary design variable in vascular modeling and regeneration.

papers.title: A Cerebral Organoid Model of Familial Alzheimer's Disease Using Amyloid Precursor Protein Mutation, Val669Leu (APP(Seoul)).
papers.summary: This study established a cerebral organoid (CO) model of familial Alzheimer's disease using the APP Val669Leu (APP(Seoul)) mutation. An hESC line overexpressing APP(Seoul) (FAD-S) produced COs showing Aβ accumulation, tau phosphorylation, and increased β-secretase expression. BACE1 inhibitor IV significantly reduced Aβ levels and tau phosphorylation in COs. Differentiated cortical neurons (FAD-S neurons) also showed elevated Aβ and phospho-tau, attenuated by BACE1 inhibitor IV. This provides 2D and 3D AD models based on the APP(Seoul) FAD mutation.

papers.title: CXCL14 Enhances Myocyte Fusion and Activates the FAK-ERK5 Signaling Pathway in Skeletal Muscle Stem Cells and Myoblasts.
papers.summary: This study investigates CXCL14 in myogenic differentiation using skeletal muscle stem cells (MuSCs) and C2C12 myoblasts. CXCL14 significantly enhanced myocyte fusion and activated the focal adhesion kinase-extracellular signal-regulated kinase 5 (FAK-ERK5) signaling pathway. The authors identified fibro-adipogenic progenitors (FAPs) as the primary source of CXCL14, revealing paracrine regulation from FAPs to MuSCs during muscle regeneration.

papers.title: Generation of a Patient-Derived Inducible Pluripotent Stem Cell Model for Studying the YARS2-Related Genetic Disease.
papers.summary: This study generated patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) models of YARS2-related genetic disease. iPSCs derived from patient Q1818 fibroblasts carry compound heterozygous YARS2 mutations (F185L/E264del); CRISPR-Cas9 produced three isogenic control lines correcting one or both mutations. Lines were validated by Sanger sequencing, stemness markers, karyotype, and trilineage differentiation. Mutations were confirmed to lie on different alleles. iPSCs differentiated into motor neurons. Four iPSC lines model this clinically severe YARS2 disease.

papers.title: A Preliminary Study on Evaluating Reparative Regeneration Potential of Human Amniotic Fluid Stem Cells Spheres in Stress Urinary Incontinence Rats.
papers.summary: This study evaluated human amniotic fluid stem cell (AFSC) spheres for stress urinary incontinence (SUI) in rats. AFSC spheres (~150 μm, minimal core necrosis, 16-20 h) had superior leak point pressure and intercontraction interval versus AFSCs, with modest/unclear myogenic gene changes but elevated secretome (VEGF, IL-6, IL-8, IL-9, MIP-1β). Bladder and external urethral sphincter histology improved, attributed to paracrine mechanisms (anti-inflammatory, angiogenic, neurotrophic) rather than myogenic differentiation.

papers.title: cP1P Maintains Long-Term Pluripotency in Human Pluripotent Stem Cells.
papers.summary: This study introduces O-cyclic phytosphingosine-1-phosphate (cP1P), a novel S1P-analog culture additive, for long-term culture of human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs). cP1P supplementation promoted long-term proliferation, upregulated pluripotency markers, and maintained trilineage differentiation capacity. RNA-seq showed cP1P alleviated long-term culture-induced upregulation of apoptosis- and chordate embryonic development-related genes while preventing downregulation of stem cell maintenance pathways, supporting hPSC proliferation, pluripotency, and differentiation during short- and long-term culture.
